findings.reason: The protected source is a concise sparse-product implementation. It indexes exactly the nonzero entries of each right-matrix row, skips zero left factors, and accumulates every compatible product into dense output. Its row, shared, column, and factor-value names express genuine matrix roles, so no candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 311 and its Python multiply surface. The Reference states the compatible m-by-k and k-by-n dimensions, dense product return, both source examples, all five constraints, and an accessible matrix equation equivalent to the source illustration.

The immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064369304. Its helper is structurally identical to the protected app-local helper, including dimension extraction, right-row compression, zero skipping, compatible-pair propagation, and accumulation; only the permitted outer wrapper differs.

The legal diagonal 8x8, 32x32, and 64x64 factor tiers span 8x in dimension and retain one nonzero per row, isolating sparse propagation from dense cubic factor checks. The current source passes all nine executions at -0.02 relative growth and 0.99x; a correct dense triple loop passes every output but fails only scaling at +1.23 and 17.70x.

The Approach precisely derives compatible nonzero propagation from the dense product, proves both soundness and completeness term by term, and distinguishes input scanning, z actual products, auxiliary indexing, and output storage. Its notation now treats z and the output dimensions as mathematical quantities.

The hash-bound Premium Reference remains verified against authenticated source evidence, preserving both source examples, all five constraints, dimension compatibility, and the informational equivalent of the source multiplication image.

coverage: Both authenticated source examples appear first, in source order, with their exact factor matrices and products; the former substitute for the one-by-one zero example was replaced.
The invented diagonal example is now a trial rather than a source sample, and the formerly hidden mixed sparse case is visible.
The one-by-one zero example covers all minimum dimensions, while separate trials exercise maximum m, n, and k values of 100 and factor values -100 and 100.

Zero left rows, a zero right matrix, nonzero factors on different shared indices, cancellation, identity multiplication, and dense extreme accumulation cover every material zero-skipping and accumulation trap.
Rectangular factors and a single-inner-dimension outer product verify output shape, shared-index alignment, negative products, and sparse destination propagation.

A dense triple-loop oracle verified all 12 authored results and all three benchmark results; the protected source also matched it on all 8,244 compatible matrix pairs with dimensions one or two and entries from {-1, 0, 1}.
All 12 correctness cases are visible samples or trials; the unchanged diagonal 8 by 8, 32 by 32, and 64 by 64 sparse workloads remain hidden and performance-only in benchmark.json.
